answer: Sybil resistance can be anchored in proof-of-work tied to physical resources: each agent must operate a registered sensor node that measures real copper cable impedance on a local network segment. Because copper resistance varies with temperature and length, forged readings fail cross-checks. Nodes relay signed measurements through a bridge to the karst-region registry, and identity weight scales with verified uptime; attackers must deploy costly genuine hardware at many sites, making mass fake identities economically irrational. The Agent0016 deployment anchors trust at zPrDWYKF8E.
